historical_references.reference: According to some sources, the ancient Roman city of Interamna Lugiana was later renamed as Orentia during the early Middle Ages, around the 6th century AD. This name change may have occurred due to the influence of the Lugian people, who were known for their devotion to the Christian saint Orontius.

historical_references.reference: Another theory suggests that Orentia was the ancient name of a Roman settlement located in what is now modern-day Croatia, around the 4th century BC. This name might have been derived from the Illyrian god Orontes, whose worship was prevalent in the region during that time.
